speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the designs of new HDB precincts have taken into account the variability and range of inclement weather, including heavy rain and strong winds; (b) whether the assessments have considered the prospects and implications of wind-swept rain entering lift shafts and affecting lift equipment; and (c) what rectification measures have been considered by HDB for new precincts where wind-swept rain has raised concerns about lift durability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) has employed various design strategies over the years to try to mitigate the extent of rainwater splashing into homes and common areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These considerations are incorporated into HDB's design requirements, to ensure that our precincts are reasonably well protected from the tropical weather even as we design for natural ventilation and ample lighting.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This allows designers to implement mitigating measures early during the design stage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB also installs rain screens and canopies at the lift lobby, if these are found to be necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These measures are generally adequate to keep rainwater out of the lift area.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have been approached by residents in Clementi Peaks, a very new precinct in Clementi.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My residents share that about one year after they moved in, HDB started installing rain shields at lift lobbies which blocked their view of the beautiful Clementi scenery.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We are told that the reason was to prevent rain entering the lift shafts, which would affect lift reliability and corrode the lifts.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My supplementary questions are, firstly, does the Minister not agree that heavy rain and strong winds are not unknown in the West of Singapore, including in Clementi?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And if there was a discovery of rain entering lift shafts during the construction phase, whether these rain shields could have been installed earlier and incorporated into the design earlier?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, we know safety is important, especially lift safety, and if there is no other option, safety must come first.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But can the Minister assure us that HDB will learn from each new development, including Clementi Peaks, so that future developments will be even better and consider climate change even more closely.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first one, he asked whether it would be possible to anticipate that there are heavy rains and strong winds, including in the Clementi area.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The answer is yes, and that is the reason why HDB has included the modelling of WDR simulations for new public housing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But in the particular case that he raised, which is I believe the case of Clementi Peaks, maybe I should explain what happened here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Before I do, let me just talk a little bit about the WDR simulations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are computational fluid dynamics, or CFD, for WDR simulations and they are conducted to meet the following HDB requirements: to identify and prevent rainwater from splashing to residential unit entrance gate and lift doors; to identify and minimise rainwater splashing to sheltered accessible routes, including drop-off porches, link bridges and linkways or void decks; and to demonstrate the effectiveness of mitigation measures proposed, such as modifying the corridor layout and/or design mitigation measures up front that will match the façade and meet the fire safety requirement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first point I want to make is that for Clementi Peaks specifically, that was before the WDR simulations were put into effect.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second point I want to make is that the works that were done were primarily for safety reason.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In short, I think we would improve the engagement process where issues like these arise in future.
